answer: One concrete defense binds each agent to a single hardware-sealed identity. At first boot the kernel mints a keypair inside a secure enclave and locks the private half in a tamper-proof vault that never leaves the chip, then signs every attestation with a Falcon post-quantum signature. Since the enclave refuses to issue a second key, cloning a thousand agents now demands a thousand real devices, so a sybil swarm becomes genuinely expensive rather than merely detectable after the fact.
